correctness.rationale: For an unselected vertex in \(A_i\), the number of selected neighbours is exactly the selected prefix count \(Y_i\); for an unselected vertex in \(B_j\), it is exactly the selected suffix count \(X_j\). This proves the full profile criterion directly. A singleton can dominate perfectly only when its own bipartition side has one vertex. With both sides of size at least two, every extreme pair \(A_p\times B_1\) works. If a selected B-vertex lies above \(B_1\), all lower A-blocks not adjacent to it must fit into the single selected A-vertex; dually for a nonextreme A-vertex. Combining the two constraints yields only the stated \(p=2\), \(\alpha_1=\beta_2=1\) exceptional nonedge. The exhaustive checker through order ten is corroborative.

final_claim: For every finite connected chain graph, perfect domination is characterized exactly by prefix and suffix selected-neighbour counts in the canonical twin classes; the minimum size is one precisely when a bipartition side is a singleton and otherwise two, with all minimum pairs and the unique exceptional nonedge family classified exactly.
limitations: Connected chain graphs and outside-only perfect domination only.
